description:
src/memory.rs:449 declares:

```
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MemoryError(
    /// Human-readable description of the underlying failure.
    pub String,
);
```

Two compounding contract issues:

1. No `#[non_exhaustive]`. Adding a structured context field (e.g. an error kind, a source-error reference, an account_id) becomes a SemVer-breaking change because all downstream code that matches on `MemoryError(s)` or constructs `MemoryError(...)` breaks at the API.

2. The inner `String` is `pub` (tuple-field accessor). Even with `#[non_exhaustive]` added, the existing field's visibility would still permit downstream code like `err.0` — locking the wire representation in.

This is `MemoryBackend::Error`, the `Self::Error` associated type used in every backend trait method signature. It is hit by every backend call site that maps backend errors to JMAP wire errors (via the workspace's `server_fail_from_backend` helper). The whole point of mapping is to insulate the JMAP wire layer from backend-specific error shapes — but a public, single-`pub String` tuple makes the backend's chosen text format an external contract.

Cookie-cutter amplification: every sibling extension-server crate has its own `MemoryError`-equivalent type. Suggested cross-check.

Fix: either
  (a) `#[non_exhaustive]` + replace tuple with a named-field struct + add accessor `pub fn description(&self) -> &str { &self.description }`, or
  (b) just add `#[non_exhaustive]` and downgrade the inner field to non-pub with an accessor.

The crate-level memory-module doc already warns "API stability is opt-in via this feature and may break across minor versions while the crate is pre-1.0" — so this is fixable. But once the crate ships 1.0, the current shape commits the maintainer to never re-shape this type.
title: MemoryError is not #[non_exhaustive] and has pub tuple field
